chunks: My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Ahmad bin Idrees, from Hussain bin Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah, and Musa bin Umar, and Hasan bin Ali bin Abi Uthman, from Ibn Sinan, that he said: I asked Abu'l-Hasan al-Rida, peace be upon him, about the noun: What is it?
He said: It is an attribute to that which is attributed.
ai.seo_question: What is the definition of a noun (ism) in Shia theological grammar?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, this hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) offers a foundational ontological definition of the noun (*ism*) as an attribute (*sifah*) inherent to a described entity (*mawsum*). This concise formulation bridges Arabic grammatical theory with Shia theological discourse, illustrating how linguistic categories are often mapped onto metaphysical realities to explain the relationship between essence and attribute.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Ahmad bin Idrees, from Hussain bin Ubaidullah, from Muhammed ibn Abdullah, and Musa bin Umar, and Hasan bin Ali bin Abi Uthman, from Ibn Sinan, that he said: I asked Abu’l-Hasan al-Rida, peace be upon him, about the noun: What is it?
He said: It is an attribute to that which is attributed.
